events.asset: MDMA (midomafetamine): Texas controlled-substance schedule placement after FDA approval
events.entity: Texas Department of State Health Services (Commissioner of Health)
events.title: Texas reschedules MDMA out of Schedule I after FDA approval
events.proposition: Texas moves MDMA (midomafetamine), or the FDA-approved MDMA drug product, out of Schedule I of the Texas Schedules of Controlled Substances into a schedule that permits prescription.
events.criterion: TRUE on the effective date of a Texas Register notice or a Texas Department of State Health Services schedule action that removes MDMA (midomafetamine) or an FDA-approved MDMA drug product from Schedule I of the Texas Schedules of Controlled Substances, or places it in Schedule II, III, IV or V. A schedule change that takes effect through the Commissioner of Health's non-objection to a federal rescheduling counts the same as any other schedule action. A federal DEA rescheduling alone, a proposal or a legislative bill does not resolve the event. Resolution source: the Texas Register (Texas Secretary of State) and the DSHS Texas Schedules of Controlled Substances page. FALSE at the deadline when no such Texas schedule action has taken effect.

resolution_source.name: Texas Register (Texas Secretary of State) and the Texas Department of State Health Services schedules of controlled substances

readings: 'Reschedule automatically' = the Texas procedure by which a federal schedule change takes effect in Texas unless the Commissioner of Health objects; the words forecast the Texas schedule outcome, and 'the Commissioner of Public Health will not object' is the mechanism, not a second event.
'If we make MDMA into a medicine' = FDA approval of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD (E-0001); the event resolves only when that condition occurs.

events.proposition: The number of treatment centers in the United States that deliver an FDA-approved psychedelic-assisted therapy is about 5,000 to 6,000 by the period end, per the named series.
events.criterion: Resolved on the named data series only: the count of US sites certified to administer an FDA-approved psychedelic-assisted therapy (an MDMA or psilocybin drug product) under that product's REMS, per the REMS program's published certified-site list, summed across approved products with duplicate sites counted once. events.title: Spravato annual sales at or above US$1 billion
events.proposition: Worldwide net sales of Spravato (esketamine nasal spray) reach at or above US$1 billion in a calendar year, per Johnson & Johnson's reported product sales.
events.criterion: Resolved on the named data series only: worldwide net trade sales of Spravato (esketamine nasal spray) in Johnson & Johnson's product-sales tables in its periodic reports on SEC EDGAR (Form 10-K and 10-Q) and the sales exhibits of its quarterly earnings releases (Form 8-K). TRUE on the date of the first Johnson & Johnson report that shows Spravato worldwide net sales at or above US$1 billion for a calendar year. 'Blockbuster' in the forecaster's words is read as US$1 billion of annual sales, the standard industry meaning, so the event resolves as binary at US$1 billion with no band. FALSE at the deadline when no completed calendar year has reached US$1 billion in the reported series. Unresolvable if the series stops and no figure has published 12 months after the deadline. Realized values are stored, not scored.

events.asset: ibogaine for a substance use disorder
events.title: FDA approval of ibogaine for a substance use disorder
events.proposition: The FDA approves an ibogaine drug product for a substance use disorder indication.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date the FDA approval letter or the Drugs@FDA entry for an ibogaine drug product with a substance use disorder indication (for example opioid, alcohol, stimulant or polysubstance use disorder) is dated, under any sponsor and with or without patents. A label for one substance use disorder counts, because the claim names the class. A complete response letter, a positive advisory vote, a filing acceptance, a breakthrough designation or an expanded-access programme is not an approval, and approval of a different molecule (for example noribogaine or another ibogaine analogue) does not count. FALSE at the deadline when no such approval is dated. Resolution source: Drugs@FDA, with the sponsor's approval announcement as a secondary source.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA; sponsor approval announcement as a secondary source

readings: 'It could go all the way through FDA approval' = the FDA approves an ibogaine product for a substance use disorder; the event is the approval itself.
'With no patents and be made available as a generic from day one' describes the intended commercial form, not a condition of the approval.
The funding condition ('if we can get the research ... fully funded') is a separate event and does not gate this one.
'Substance use disorders' is a class, so a label for any one substance use disorder counts.
